chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

The best traits of women are the worst traits of men: vanity, cowardice, and miserliness. Thus, when the woman is vain, she does not allow anyone access to herself; when she is miserly, she preserves her property and her husband's property; and when she is cowardly, she fears everything that befalls her.

key_terms.الزَّهْوُ: Vanity or pride, here interpreted as a trait that leads to modesty and exclusivity in women
key_terms.الْبُخْلُ: Miserliness or stinginess, interpreted here as careful preservation of wealth
key_terms.الْجُبْنُ: Cowardice or timidity, interpreted here as a cautious nature

ai.seo_question: What are the best traits of women according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) presents a nuanced view of gender-specific virtues in Nahj al-Balagha, where traits often considered negative in men—vanity, cowardice, and miserliness—are recontextualized as protective qualities for women. This perspective reflects the traditional sociological understanding of his time, where 'vanity' (al-zahw) implies a dignified reserve that prevents easy access, 'miserliness' (al-bukhl) ensures financial stewardship of the household, and 'cowardice' (al-jubn) denotes a cautious wariness of external threats. This interpretation highlights how ethical virtues are not absolute but are evaluated based on their functional impact within specific social and familial roles.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 234. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

The best traits of women are those which are the worst traits of men, namely: vanity, cowardice and miserliness. Thus, since the woman is vain, she will not allow anyone access to herself; since she is miserly, she will preserve her own property and the property of her husband; and since she is weak-hearted, she will be frightened with everything that befalls her.
